body:
GTCR disclosed in a regulatory filing that it is weighing a buyout of Global Payments, though it has made no definitive decision. Bloomberg reported the transaction could be worth about $50 billion, including debt and a premium.

GTCR holds a 16% stake in Global Payments, acquired last year when it sold 55% of Worldpay to the company, giving it significant influence over any deal. The move follows the dropping of an earlier joint effort with CD&R, and comes as Global Payments faces slowing growth in some business lines, heavier competition and investor pressure for greater profitability.

GTCR's 16% stake is the largest held in Global Payments, and the reported $50 billion transaction value compares with the company's $24.3 billion market value after its 10% share rise Friday. Whether GTCR proceeds with an offer has not been determined.

GTCR is a private equity firm that is Global Payments' largest shareholder with a 16% stake acquired through the Worldpay transaction.

Global Payments is a publicly traded payments technology company that acquired Worldpay in April 2025.

Clayton, Dubilier & Rice is a private equity firm that reportedly teamed with GTCR on an earlier joint bid for Global Payments before the effort was dropped.

GTCR disclosed its evaluation of the move in a regulatory filing, days after reports that its consortium effort with CD&R had been dropped. Global Payments' shares rose 10% on Friday, and the company had completed its April 2025 acquisition of Worldpay, with a net price of $22.7 billion, while selling its Issuer Solutions business to FIS for $13.5 billion.

April 2025: Global Payments acquired Worldpay and sold its Issuer Solutions business to FIS.

Last year: GTCR acquired its 16% Global Payments stake through the Worldpay sale.

Oct. 30, 2026: GTCR and CD&R were reported to have teamed up on a joint bid to buy out Global Payments.

Friday, Nov. 20, 2026: Bloomberg and Reuters reported the buyout valuation, and Global Payments shares rose 10%.

The potential takeover fits into a broader pattern of private equity firms seeking control of large payments companies as competitive pressure and investor demands for profitability intensify. It follows directly from Global Payments' 2025 Worldpay transaction, which reshaped its business mix and ownership.

Shareholders of Global Payments could see a change in the stock's value if a buyout proceeds at the reported valuation, while the 10% share rise already reflects investor expectations. Retail investors holding the stock should watch for a definitive GTCR announcement, since no decision has been made.

A potential Global Payments buyout will be tested commercially, as merchant customers will judge whether service quality holds up through a change in ownership. Investors and customers alike should track whether GTCR moves from evaluation to a definitive offer.

For more on deals of this kind, see the Corporate Finance section.
